text:
aj: Heads up — after the kernel-selection tweak rolled at 9649990000 I'm seeing a p95 tail bump on the streaming chat route. Short prompts hit ~34ms p95 (was ~28ms).

maria: Which route and payload size?

aj: streaming.chat.fast, avg prompt ~20 tokens, payloads ~300 bytes. Repro on canary. CPU sampling points to host-side parse/demux increase.

aj: quick flame excerpt from host sampler:
```
parse_total: 1.72ms
  - proto_unwrap: 0.42ms
  - demux: 0.68ms
  - hpack_decode: 0.18ms
  - copy/serialize: 0.44ms
kv_cache_probe: 0.12ms
kernel_select: 0.06ms
```

sasha: interesting. demux nearly doubled compared to baseline traces. Did the selector start doing any pre-normalization or frame reassembly on host?

aj: Yes — new selector tries to pre-merge small windows to favor a larger kernel path. I think that adds an extra copy/scan for tiny payloads.

kevin: Could also be more writev/syscall churn on the streaming path — if demux alters framing we might be doing extra iov aggregation. Have microbench?

maria: I ran dedicated microbench against a 20-token payload. Baseline (old selector): p95 parse 0.9ms. With selector: p95 parse 1.8ms. So it's consistent.

aj: Repro script used (local dev):
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  echo -n "POST payload" | ./curl-stream --http2 --streaming \
    -H 'content-type: application/proto' \
    --data-binary @- http://localhost:8080/v1/stream
done
```

sasha: Can you capture strace on the host to confirm writev counts? Also capture ingress proxy logs for smallwrite coalescing.

aj: grabbed a small strace: average writev calls per request went 1 -> 3 for tiny responses. Looks like demux/merge logic causes split writes.

ingest-bot: deploy-bot: rollout v2.3-selector to canary at 9649990000, 40% hosts.

kevin: So two costs: (1) added CPU in parse/demux due to pre-merge scanning, (2) syscall+writev churn. Both hurt short prompt latency.

maria: Proposal: gate pre-merge to only trigger for payloads > 2kb OR when sequence length > 256. Quick canary tweak and measure.

aj: I built a quick patch to bypass demux pre-merge for payloads < 1024 bytes. Local bench shows p95 parse back to 0.95ms and overall p95 to ~29ms.

sasha: Nice. Can you open a small PR with perf numbers + microbench script? We'll run on canary 40% and watch p95 and writev metrics.

aj: On it. PR will include perf csv and the strace sample.

kevin: Also let's add a kernel-selector unit test that asserts we don't do an extra copy for tiny frames. Prevent regression.

maria: Agreed. Follow-up: quick 15m triage tomorrow 10:15 PT to decide revert vs tweak if canary doesn't improve.

aj: ping @sasha @kevin I'll post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:

sasha: Thanks — if canary shows variance, we may need a fallback policy to prefer old selector for short-llm workloads.

kevin: Also check KV cache hit patterns — if demux changes key normalization we might see subtle evictions, but so far kv_probe looks tiny.

maria: Good catch. For now action items: aj -> PR + bench, sasha -> writev/strace comparison on canary hosts, kevin -> add unit test and monitor kv metrics. Meeting tomorrow 10:15 PT.

aj: Updated: PR created 9654321022 -> https://git.internal/r/ingress/PR/458 (bench attached).

sasha: Kicking off canary run with the patch at 9654321030. Will post telemetry.

kevin: 👍

maria: closing the loop later today. thanks everyone.
